prompts: A patient brought lab exam PDFs from two different labs, months apart; they are in {WS}/exams. Build one history per marker, every value in the units of the first report, and say what got worse. Record in {WS}/result.json: history (marker -> {date: value}) and worse (a list of the markers that got worse and are now outside the first report's reference range).
answers:
[goal] Build one history per marker from the two lab PDFs in ./exams, in the first report's units, and record worse markers in ./result.json.

[action] Extracted both PDFs via pdftotext (verified with the PDF text), read dates/markers/ranges, converted Beta values to Alfa units, wrote ./result.json.

[result] ./result.json holds history per marker (dates 2026-02-10 for Alfa, 2026-08-18 for Beta, collection dates) and "worse" = Glicose em jejum and Colesterol LDL, both now outside the Alfa reference ranges (glucose 109.9 mg/dL vs 70–99; LDL 143.1 mg/dL vs <130). Creatinina improved (0.95→0.86 mg/dL, within 0.70–1.30); HbA1c rose 5.4→5.54% but stays inside 4.0–5.6%, so it is not in "worse".

[next] Assumptions: Alfa is the first report (dated 10/02/2026, values in mg/dL and %, the unit set kept); Beta (18/08/2026 collection) converted with standard factors — glucose ×18.018 mg/dL per mmol/L, LDL cholesterol ×38.67, creatinine ÷88.4 µmol/L per mg/dL, HbA1c (37 mmol/mol → 5.54%, IFCC formula % = (mmol/mol + 23.5)/10.93). "Worse" = value increased (all four markers are "lower is better") AND now outside the first report's range; dates in the history are the collection dates (Alfa "Data da coleta", Beta "Coleta"), ISO format. No tabs/apps were opened and none need closing.

Values were computed, not invented; both source PDFs were read directly before conversion.
